screening_decisions.reason: Prospective pelvic mass cohort; pre-diagnostic serum HE4 and CA125 assessed; multivariable indices (ROMA, RMI combining menopausal status, USS, CA-125) compared against final diagnosis/histology. Fits DTA in adnexal masses with appropriate reference standard.
Prospective cross-sectional DTA; women undergoing surgery for pelvic mass; HE4, CA125, and ROMA compared with final pathological results. Matches target population and index tests.

Diagnostic accuracy study; IOTA ADNEX (ultrasound-based with/without CA-125) evaluated in adnexal masses; all underwent surgery with histopathology reference. Relevant multivariable model combining ultrasound and biomarker.
Retrospective audit of CA125 usage across mixed patients (including males); not a DTA study of pelvic masses and lacks consistent reference standard. Wrong population/design.
Retrospective DTA using prospectively collected data; adnexal masses with pathology reference; compares ADNEX, RMI, LR2, and other ultrasound models. Meets DTA criteria.
Systematic review/meta-analysis; not a primary DTA study.
Surgically managed adnexal masses; RMI 1–4 evaluated (combines menopausal status, ultrasound, CA-125) with histopathology as endpoint. Appropriate DTA design.
Prospective multicenter evaluation of HE4, CA125, and ROMA in discriminating benign pelvic mass vs EOC with menopausal subgrouping. DTA of relevant biomarkers/algorithms in adnexal mass context.

Evaluates HE4, CA125, and ROMA across healthy, benign gynecologic diseases, and cancers including ovarian; although not limited to pelvic masses and reference standard for benign disease is unclear, it assesses relevant biomarkers for OC discrimination.
Systematic review on symptoms; not a DTA study of menopausal status/USS/biomarkers or multivariable models in pelvic masses.
Systematic review/meta-analysis; not primary DTA research.
Epidemiological burden report; not a DTA study, wrong focus.
Prospective multicentre diagnostic study; ADNEX model uses clinical+ultrasound+CA-125; histology as reference; directly within scope for adnexal masses.
Retrospective surgical series with histology; compares CA-125, HE4, ROMA, RMI-II in adnexal masses with menopausal subgroup analyses. Fits DTA criteria.
Prospective case–control including women with adnexal masses; evaluates HE4+CA125 and ROMA with ROC analyses. Preoperative biomarker DTA relevant to target setting, though design is case–control.

Assesses diagnostic discrimination of HE4/CA-125/ROMA across benign conditions and EOC with validated cutoffs; includes prognostic analyses. Population overlaps adnexal masses; diagnostic component relevant though reference standards for benign groups unclear.
Prospective multicentre DTA; compares IOTA ultrasound strategies and RMI; histology reference standard. Directly addresses comparative test accuracy in adnexal masses.
Original RMI DTA study; combines CA-125, ultrasound, and menopausal status; benign vs malignant pelvic masses with histology reference. Core to review objective.
Basic science/immunohistochemistry tissue expression study; not a clinical DTA study in symptomatic women with pelvic masses.
Clinical comparison of CA125, HE4, and ROMA with subgrouping by menopausal status and pathologic types; implies pathology reference; relevant DTA of biomarker combinations.
Prospective cohort of women with suspicious cystic ovarian masses scheduled for operation; preoperative HE4 and CA-125 measured; histology reference. Fits DTA in target population.

Evaluates HE4, CA125, and ROMA in benign gynecologic diseases, ovarian cancer, and healthy women; provides DTA metrics; although not restricted to adnexal masses and reference standards for benign may be mixed, diagnostic component is relevant.
Prospective multicentre validation of ultrasound-based rules in adnexal masses with histology reference; aligns with ultrasound component of review.
Cross-sectional DTA of ROMA (CA125+HE4) in postmenopausal women with pelvic masses; histology used as reference.
Incidence/mortality projections; not a diagnostic test accuracy study in pelvic masses.
Qualitative experiences; not diagnostic test accuracy.
Narrative/basic science review; not diagnostic test accuracy.
General-population screening biomarker lead-time; not DTA in symptomatic pelvic masses.
Methodological tool paper (QUADAS-2); not primary diagnostic accuracy.
Cross-sectional validation of ROMA (CA125+HE4+menopause) in pelvic masses; histology reference.
Literature review of CA125; not primary diagnostic accuracy in target population.
Pathogenesis review; not a diagnostic test accuracy study.
Proteomics review; not diagnostic accuracy in women with pelvic masses.
DTA of RMI (ultrasound+menopausal status+CA125) versus histopathology in adnexal masses.
Cross-sectional DTA of ROMA in pelvic masses; biopsy/clinical follow-up as reference.
Cross-sectional DTA comparing ultrasound, CA125, RMI and combinations in adnexal masses; surgical histology reference.
Cross-sectional DTA of IOTA ultrasound rules; histologic reference standard.
Meta-research on publication bias methods; not primary diagnostic accuracy.
Cross-sectional DTA of HE4, CA125, ROMA in pelvic masses; histologic reference.
External validation of IOTA ADNEX multivariable ultrasound model against histology.
Service evaluation of symptom-triggered testing; not diagnostic accuracy in pelvic masses.
Prospective DTA of HE4+CA125 algorithm by menopausal status in pelvic masses; surgical histology reference.
Practice guideline on adnexal masses; not a diagnostic accuracy study.
Molecular genetics of ARID1A; not diagnostic accuracy.
Narrative review of HE4; not a diagnostic test accuracy study.
Prospective DTA of HE4 and ROMA in pelvic masses with surgical reference.
Population registry incidence trends; no diagnostic index tests (USS/biomarkers/models) and no diagnostic accuracy design or reference standard for adnexal masses.
Systematic review/meta-analysis; not a primary diagnostic accuracy or validation study within the target population.
Prospective DTA of ROMA (HE4+CA-125, menopausal status) in women with adnexal masses; histopathology used as reference standard; aligns with index tests and target population.

Prospective cross-sectional validation of IOTA LR2, Simple Rules, RMI, and subjective assessment in women with adnexal masses; surgical histology reference; directly relevant multivariable models/USS.
Meta-analysis; not a primary study in the screening stage.
Prospective cross-sectional DTA in patients with adnexal masses; evaluates CA-125, HE4, ROMA, RMI; histopathology as gold standard; matches target tests and population.
Multicenter study of HE4, CA-125, ROMA in women with suspicious pelvic masses requiring surgery; histologically verified; aligns with index tests and population.
Methodological paper on meta-analysis modeling; not a DTA study of the target tests/population.
Simulation/methods study; no primary DTA data in the target population or tests.
Genetic predisposition study; not evaluating diagnostic tests (USS/biomarkers/combined models) for adnexal masses against histology/follow-up.
Narrative review on prevention/detection/treatment; not a primary DTA study in the target setting.
Prospective, multicenter, blinded validation of ROMA (HE4+CA-125) in women with pelvic/adnexal masses; histology reference; directly addresses index tests and population.
Prospective comparison of RMI indices in women with pelvic masses undergoing surgery; histology as reference; evaluates validated multivariable models using menopausal status, USS, CA-125.
Postmenopausal women with adnexal masses undergoing surgery; evaluates RMI and CA-125 (eligible index tests) with histopathology; fits cross-sectional DTA design.

Assesses HE4, CA-125, ROMA preoperatively in women with benign disease vs epithelial ovarian cancer; diagnostic performance reported and consistent with histological classification; aligns with eligible index tests.
Primary care symptom-based case-control without focus on women with a confirmed pelvic mass or on the specified index tests; not a DTA study with histology/follow-up reference.
Prospective validation of ROMA in women with a pelvic mass scheduled for surgery; evaluates HE4 and CA-125 with histological outcomes; matches eligible tests and design.
Systematic review/meta-analysis of models; not a primary validation study within this screening stage.
Cross-sectional comparison of CA-125, HE4, ROMA, and RMI in patients with ovarian masses; diagnostic performance reported; aligns with index tests and population.
Guideline/commentary on hereditary risk; not a DTA study of adnexal masses using the specified index tests and reference standards.
Cross-sectional study in women with ovarian masses; CA-125, HE4, ROMA measured preoperatively and compared with postoperative histopathology; eligible tests and design.
Postmenopausal cohort with ovarian masses; evaluates HE4, CA-125, ROMA2; all diagnoses histologically verified; aligns with index tests and target population.

Postmenopausal/perimenopausal women with suspected ovarian tumors; evaluates 2D USS, 3D power Doppler, CA-125, RMI, IOTA Simple Rules, LR2 vs histopathology; directly relevant multivariable/USS-based tests.
Systematic review/meta-analysis comparing HE4 vs CA-125; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study in a pelvic mass cohort.

Primary diagnostic accuracy study in 129 women with suspected pelvic mass scheduled for surgery/biopsy; evaluates HE4, CA125, and ROMA with sensitivity/specificity and ROC (histology-based reference).
Prospective comparison in women presenting with complex pelvic mass; evaluates HE4, CA125, ROMA, and RMI vs histology with diagnostic metrics.
Methodological tool (PROBAST) for risk of bias assessment; not a primary DTA study nor specific to ovarian masses.
Women with pelvic mass scheduled for surgery; evaluates ROMA (HE4+CA125) with separate pre/postmenopausal performance vs histology.
Epidemiological ‘routes to diagnosis’ across cancers; not a diagnostic test accuracy evaluation for ovarian masses.
Statistical methodology paper on bivariate meta-analysis; no primary patient-level diagnostic evaluation.
Prospective, population-based cohort of women with a pelvic mass scheduled for surgery; compares RMI vs ROMA, CA125 vs HE4 with diagnostic metrics vs pathology.
Software user guide for meta-analysis (MetaDAS); no primary DTA data in ovarian mass population.
Meta-analysis comparing ROMA, HE4, CA125; secondary research, not a primary diagnostic study.
Multicenter IOTA database analysis of adnexal masses with histology reference; evaluates IOTA models, simple rules, and RMI diagnostic performance.
Subset analysis from a prospective trial of women undergoing surgery for an adnexal mass (premenopausal); evaluates HE4 and CA-125 vs histology.
Case-control/prognostic focus (EOC patients vs controls) and therapy-monitoring; not a DTA study in symptomatic women with pelvic masses.
Benign gynecologic disorders only; does not assess diagnostic accuracy for malignancy vs histology in a pelvic mass cohort.
Narrative/overview review of biomarkers; not a primary DTA study.
Biomarker development/case-control assay validation (HE4) in carcinoma patients vs controls; not a cross-sectional pelvic mass DTA study.
Systematic review of prediction models; secondary research, not primary DTA.
Endometrial cancer sentinel lymph node DTA; different target condition than ovarian cancer.
Paper includes a prospective validation study of IOTA simple rules against histology (in addition to a meta-analysis); single-test ultrasound DTA within adnexal tumors fits inclusion.

Diagnostic performance study of CA125, HE4, and ROMA with pre/postmenopausal analyses; likely compares to pathology though population includes benign gynecologic disease; include conservatively at title/abstract.
Review of diagnostic indices; secondary research without primary patient-level DTA data.
Multicenter clinical trial in women with unknown ovarian cyst/pelvic tumor; preop biomarkers + ultrasound parameters vs final pathology (RMI, ROMA, CA125, HE4).
Clinical cohort of 353 women undergoing adnexal surgery; validates ADNEX ultrasound model vs subjective assessment with histology reference; appropriate single-test DTA.
